around.headline: Three domestic-dispute deaths in Bengaluru inside 48 hours
around.summary: An auto driver stabbed his wife to death before ending his life (Sept 9), a man killed his wife with a beer bottle before dying by suicide (Sept 10), and a couple was found dead at home in a suspected family dispute (Sept 9), per The Hindu, TOI and NDTV. If you or someone you know is in an escalating domestic situation, involve the police (100) or a women's helpline (1091) early, rather than waiting for it to boil over.

around.headline: One card, one app now covers both Namma Metro and BMTC buses
around.summary: Bengaluru has rolled out a single card usable across Namma Metro and BMTC, alongside a new 'Namma BMTC 2.0' app and WhatsApp-based ticketing for bus travel, per Moneycontrol and The Indian Express. Worth switching over if you regularly hop between metro and bus — one less card or ticket to juggle.

around.headline: UK air-traffic glitch disrupts flights — a Bengaluru-London Air India service was diverted to Vienna
around.summary: A technical glitch in UK air traffic control disrupted flights to and from India, with an Air India Bengaluru-London flight diverted to Vienna and some return legs cancelled, per Deccan Herald and The New Indian Express. If you're flying to or from the UK in the next day or two, check your flight status before heading to the airport.
around.source: Deccan Herald, The New Indian Express

around.headline: SIR flags anomalies for 6.24 lakh Bengaluru voters, no-mapping notices for 18 lakh more
around.summary: Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls has flagged anomalies for 6.24 lakh Bengaluru voters and issued 'no-mapping' notices to another 18 lakh, and officials say they'll only visit homes in person for VIP voters, per The New Indian Express and The Hindu. It's worth checking your own voter-roll status online rather than assuming a physical visit will catch any issue with yours.
around.source: The New Indian Express, The Hindu

around.headline: CM hints at a tunnel road to bypass Lalbagh
around.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar has hinted at a new tunnel-road alignment designed to route traffic around Lalbagh instead of through it, per The News Minute. It's an early-stage idea, not a confirmed plan yet, so don't expect construction to start soon.

around.headline: Multiplexes challenge Karnataka's 2% ticket cess in court
around.summary: Multiplex operators have moved the Karnataka High Court against a 2% cess added to movie tickets, per TOI Bengaluru. Until the case is resolved, expect the cess to still show up on your ticket price at the multiplex.

around.headline: India hosts the BRICS summit as China confirms Xi Jinping will visit after 7 years
around.summary: India is hosting the BRICS summit even as the Iran war tests the bloc's unity, and China has confirmed President Xi Jinping will visit India for the first time in seven years to discuss trade and normalising ties, per Reuters and The Hindu. A genuine thaw in India-China relations could eventually ease friction for Bengaluru's tech and electronics sector, which relies heavily on Chinese components and capital equipment.

street_smart.title: You're at a crowded Bengaluru mall food court when a middle-aged man at the next table suddenly clutches his chest, gasps, and collapses to the floor. He doesn't respond when people call his name. What's the smartest first move?
street_smart.based_on: No incident in today's feeds fits the choice-based trap format cleanly — today's real news (three separate domestic-dispute deaths, a vet clinic raided for animal cruelty, SIR voter-roll anomalies, a proposed tunnel road) is either tragedy-driven or civic/administrative rather than a personal decision point. Rotating in from the evergreen list: medical emergency response (108, CPR basics), which hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks — the closest recent entry, the hidden-pothole accident (Sept 6 morning), was about civic-negligence compensation and hospital billing, not bystander first-response.
street_smart.situation: A small crowd starts gathering and phones come out to film, but no one has stepped in yet.

choices.text: Call 108 immediately (or get someone else to call while you act), check if he's breathing normally, and if not, start hands-only chest compressions — push hard and fast in the centre of his chest — until help arrives or he responds.
choices.feedback: Correct. 108 is Karnataka's free ambulance service, and in cardiac arrest, survival odds drop roughly 10% for every minute without circulation — hands-only CPR doesn't require certification and is exactly what bystander guidelines recommend until trained help takes over.

choices.text: Loosen his collar, prop him up against a chair, and try to get him to sip some water to help him 'come around.'
choices.feedback: This is the trap. An unresponsive or semi-conscious person can't reliably protect their airway, so water can go into the lungs instead of the stomach and cause choking or aspiration — propping him up doesn't fix a lack of circulation either; what he needs is compressions and oxygen, not fluids.

choices.text: Wait for mall security or a doctor to arrive before touching him, since you're not trained in CPR and don't want to make things worse.
choices.feedback: Risky. Hesitation costs the exact minutes that matter most in cardiac arrest, and hands-only CPR (just chest compressions, no mouth-to-mouth needed) is simple enough for an untrained bystander to do safely — waiting idle is worse than trying.

choices.text: Shake him vigorously and shout to wake him up, and if that doesn't work, try to carry him to your car to rush him to the nearest hospital yourself.
choices.feedback: Risky. Moving an unresponsive person alone interrupts any chance of starting compressions and risks injuring him further, and a private car can't do what an ambulance can — 108 paramedics arrive equipped to treat him en route and can alert the hospital before you even get there.

takeaways: For a collapsed, unresponsive person: call 108 (Karnataka's free ambulance) or get a bystander to call, then check breathing before doing anything else.
Hands-only CPR — fast, hard compressions in the centre of the chest — needs no certification and is what most bystanders should do until paramedics take over.
Never give food, water or medicine to someone who is unresponsive or only semi-conscious — they can't protect their airway and may choke or aspirate it.

quiz.question: Karnataka's ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has flagged anomalies for roughly how many Bengaluru voters?
quiz.why: A separate 18 lakh voters got 'no-mapping' notices, meaning their address couldn't be matched to existing rolls — officials say they'll only visit homes in person for VIP voters, so it's worth checking your own status online.

quiz.question: What new travel option did Bengaluru commuters gain this week across Namma Metro and BMTC buses?
options: Nothing changed — separate cards are still required
A single card usable across both Metro and BMTC
A week of free travel citywide
WhatsApp booking only, with no physical card option
quiz.why: The rollout came alongside a new 'Namma BMTC 2.0' app and WhatsApp-based bus ticketing — part of a broader push to unify transit payments the way common mobility cards already work in several other Indian cities.

quiz.question: Which world leader is set to visit India after a seven-year gap, as confirmed by China ahead of the BRICS summit?
quiz.why: Xi Jinping's last visit to India was the 2019 informal summit in Mahabalipuram, near Chennai — this trip is expected to focus on trade and normalising ties after years of border tension.

quiz.question: Under India's Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher for the Rajya Sabha — 30 years — reflecting its design as the more experience-weighted upper house.

quiz.question: Roughly how high above sea level does Bengaluru sit?
quiz.why: That elevation on the Deccan plateau is a big reason Bengaluru's climate stays milder year-round than most Indian metros closer to sea level.
